Rep. Norma Torres highlights community initiatives and pays tribute to Dolores Huerta
Rep. Norma Torres marked October 28 with tributes to activist Dolores Huerta and announcements about local projects such as Cypress Grove Supportive Housing in Fontana.
Rep. Norma Torres, a U.S. Congresswoman representing California’s 35th district since 2015, shared several updates on her official Twitter account on October 28, 2026.
In a message posted at 17:29 UTC, Torres expressed her condolences following the death of labor leader Dolores Huerta: "I am heartbroken by the passing of Dolores Huerta, a woman I deeply admired and whose courage paved the way for generations of Latinas like me. As a Latina and immigrant, I know that I stand on the shoulders of women like Dolores, who refused to be silenced and made sure our".
Later that day at 20:07 UTC, Torres announced progress on an affordable housing initiative in Fontana: "Exciting news for Fontana! Today, I was thrilled to break ground on Cypress Grove Supportive Housing! This project will bring 39 new units of affordable housing tailored specifically for individuals with disabilities. A huge thank you to Fontana’s mayor, city council, and".
At 21:49 UTC, she encouraged constituents to access resources related to voting rights: "Every eligible voter deserves clear answers and protected rights. Download our 'Voting Know Your Rights' card at https://t.co/fW0xc79u1C to stay informed and protect your vote! #InlandEmpire #KnowYourRights #ProtectTheVote https://t.co/O6WltjyND7".
Torres has represented California’s 35th District in Congress since succeeding Gloria Negrete McLeod in 2015. She previously served in both the California State Assembly (2008-2013) and California Senate (2013-2014). Born in Escuintla, Guatemala in 1965, Torres resides in Pomona and holds a BA from National Labor College.
